facts.text: Begin expert consultation with independent structured interviews rather than a workshop, and assess individual claims rather than the expert's authority.
facts.quote: Begin with independent structured interviews and make the unit of analysis the claim, not the expert's authority.

facts.text: Group discussion can create premature convergence, status effects and hidden disagreement during expert consultation.
facts.quote: Group discussion creates premature convergence, status effects and hidden disagreement.

facts.text: For each important expert assertion, ask for the exact belief, supporting evidence, confidence or range, necessary assumptions, evidence that would change the expert's mind, opposing expert views and someone else who could validate the claim.
facts.quote: What exactly do you believe? What evidence supports it? What is your confidence or range? What assumptions make it true? What evidence would change your mind? What would an expert who disagrees say? Who else should validate this claim?

facts.text: The Critical Decision Method, described by Klein, Calderwood and MacGregor (1989) and Crandall, Klein and Hoffman (2006), elicits judgment from specific past cases rather than general opinions.
facts.quote: The Critical Decision Method (Klein, Calderwood and MacGregor, 1989; Crandall, Klein and Hoffman, 2006) elicits judgment from specific past cases rather than general opinions

facts.text: A Critical Decision Method interview can ask what happened the last time a sensor model failed to match field data, rather than asking generally how reliable sensor models are.
facts.quote: ask "the last time a sensor model failed to match field data, what happened?" rather than "how reliable are sensor models?"

facts.text: Bogner, Littig and Menz (2009) cover expert interviewing as a research method.
facts.quote: Bogner, Littig and Menz (2009) cover expert interviewing as a research method [214].

facts.text: Cooke's Classical Model (1991) weights experts according to their performance on calibration questions.
facts.quote: Cooke's Classical Model (1991) weights experts by their performance on calibration questions [215].

facts.text: Colson and Cooke's 2018 review of 33 applications found substantial variation in expert calibration.
facts.quote: Colson and Cooke (2018) reviewed 33 applications and found substantial variation in expert calibration

facts.text: In Colson and Cooke's 2018 review, fewer than one third of individual experts met the study's statistical-accuracy criterion; expertise alone therefore does not guarantee accurate uncertainty estimates.
facts.quote: fewer than one third of individual experts met the study's statistical-accuracy criterion, so expertise alone does not guarantee accurate uncertainty estimates [50].

facts.text: Colson and Cooke's 2017 cross-validation study found expert performance weighting strong in-sample but documented an out-of-sample penalty.
facts.quote: Their cross-validation study (2017) found performance weighting strong in-sample but documented an out-of-sample penalty [216].

facts.text: The IDEA protocol (Hemming and colleagues, 2018), the SHELF framework (O'Hagan and colleagues, 2006) and EFSA's 2014 guidance provide practical procedures for structured elicitation of quantities.
facts.quote: The IDEA protocol (Hemming and colleagues, 2018), the SHELF framework (O'Hagan and colleagues, 2006) and EFSA's 2014 guidance are the practical procedures [217, 218, 219].

facts.text: Rowe and Wright (1999) found that Delphi generally outperforms unstructured groups, but consensus does not establish correctness.
facts.quote: Delphi generally beats unstructured groups (Rowe and Wright, 1999), but consensus is not correctness

facts.text: Methodological reviews published between 2021 and 2024 note wide variation in the design and reporting of Delphi studies; no single review was identified.
facts.quote: methodological reviews published between 2021 and 2024 note wide variation in how Delphi studies are designed and reported (no single review was identified) [220].

facts.text: Training and teaming improved forecasting accuracy in geopolitical forecasting tournaments reported by Mellers and colleagues (2014).
facts.quote: Training and teaming improved forecasting accuracy in the geopolitical forecasting tournaments (Mellers and colleagues, 2014) [221].

facts.text: The evidence supports structured elicitation of expert judgment.
facts.quote: Verdict: structured elicitation is supported.

facts.text: For estimates of durations, model errors and likelihoods, calibrate expert judgment against historical or known-answer questions wherever practical.
facts.quote: For durations, model errors and likelihoods, calibrate expert judgment against historical or known-answer questions where practical

facts.text: When expert judgment cannot be calibrated, record ranges and disagreement instead of averaging opinions into an apparently precise number.
facts.quote: where calibration is impossible, record ranges and disagreement rather than averaging opinions into an apparently precise number.

facts.text: The UK Ministry of Defence Red Teaming Handbook, third edition (2021), documents red-teaming practice.
facts.quote: Documented practice includes the UK Ministry of Defence Red Teaming Handbook (3rd edition, 2021)

facts.text: The U.S. Army Red Team Handbook documents red-teaming practice.
facts.quote: the U.S. Army Red Team Handbook

facts.text: Zenko's survey documents red-teaming practice.
facts.quote: Zenko's survey of red-teaming practice

facts.text: Shipley colour-team proposal reviews are a documented review practice supported by vendor evidence.
facts.quote: Shipley colour-team proposal reviews

facts.text: NASA Standing Review Boards are a documented review practice.
facts.quote: NASA Standing Review Boards

facts.text: UK Gateway Reviews are a documented review practice.
facts.quote: UK Gateway Reviews

facts.text: Fagan inspections are a documented review practice.
facts.quote: Fagan inspections

facts.text: A red team should not edit grammar; give the red team an adversarial charter to demonstrate that the plan cannot support its stated safety claim by the deadline.
facts.quote: The red team should not edit grammar; give it an adversarial charter: "Demonstrate that this plan cannot support its stated safety claim by the deadline."

facts.text: Ask a plan's red team to attack scope, hidden assumptions, architecture, reference data, acceptance thresholds, schedule logic, resource availability, integration dependencies, standards interpretation, evidence independence, scenario coverage, model extrapolation, fallback feasibility and executive claims.
facts.quote: attack scope, hidden assumptions, architecture, reference data, acceptance thresholds, schedule logic, resource availability, integration dependencies, standards interpretation, evidence independence, scenario coverage, model extrapolation, fallback feasibility and the executive claims.

facts.text: Red teams are established practice in security, defence and proposal review.
facts.quote: Red teams are established practice in security, defence and proposal review

facts.text: No direct controlled evidence was found that a red-team review improves schedule or safety performance in an engineering capability programme.
facts.quote: direct controlled evidence that a red-team review improves schedule or safety performance in an engineering capability programme was not found.

facts.text: Dialectical inquiry and devil's advocacy produced better decisions than consensus approaches in laboratory studies reported by Schweiger, Sandberg and Ragan (1986) and Schwenk's 1990 meta-analysis.
facts.quote: Dialectical inquiry and devil's advocacy produced better decisions than consensus approaches in laboratory studies (Schweiger, Sandberg and Ragan, 1986; Schwenk's 1990 meta-analysis)

facts.text: Nemeth, Brown and Rogers (2001) found that authentic dissent outperforms an assigned devil's advocate.
facts.quote: authentic dissent beats an assigned devil's advocate (Nemeth, Brown and Rogers, 2001) [227, 228, 51].

facts.text: Recruit real skeptics for structured challenge rather than appointing someone to play a skeptic.
facts.quote: Recruit real skeptics rather than appointing one.
